# Sci-fi cartoon — Style Prompt

> Adult-animation sci-fi sitcom: thick boiling outlines, flat colour, a duo whose reactions don't match, one glowing portal, and one palette per world. The comedy lives in faces and silences, not in movement.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

Hand-drawn-looking 2D TV animation for grown-ups: **uniform thick dark outlines that boil**, **flat fills with hard-edged shadow shapes (no gradients)**, **big white eyes with tiny pupils**, **elastic mouths**, and sci-fi hardware treated like household junk. The engine of the genre is **a tiny, mundane goal pursued with absurdly large means**: a gate between worlds used to get one cardboard robot to a school match. The joke is the difference between two reactions: one lead deadpan with heavy lids, the other panicking, sweating and trembling.

Not a kids' cartoon (dry humour, long pauses), not anime (no sparkly eyes), not a vector explainer (nothing is ever perfectly still: lines boil even in a held pose).

Invent your own cast, props and travel device. No existing show's characters, silhouettes, colour pairings, catchphrases or portal gun.

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Line**: near-black, 7 px for characters and props, 4–6 px for background detail, round joins. **Line width is constant in screen space**: a close-up is redrawn larger at the same weight (`vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke`), never scaled into a fat line.
- **Boil**: resample every outline every ~7 px and displace along the normal with low-frequency noise, amplitude about 1.7 px, in **3 drawings cycling at 12 fps**. Build the three drawings once as three path variants and swap them with one attribute on the root: nothing is redrawn per frame.
- **Fill**: flat colours only. Shadows are hard-edged darker shapes (a translucent mix of the line colour) on the side away from the light. Glows are one or two flat translucent rings. Walls and floors are flat bands.
- **The lab is busy**: the film lives in a set full of repeated, simple things. Draw one object once and repeat it (a long shelf of coloured flasks), and give the set a bench machine with a small face screen, a potted plant, a wall clock and a dark chalkboard whose chalk is the wall colour. Keep it flat and behind the leads.
- **Faces**: big white eyes touching or almost, 5 px pupils, heavy lids for deadpan, brows carrying the emotion (flat and low for deadpan, inner ends raised for worry). Two mouth states per character, closed line and open mouth with teeth and tongue, swapped on twos.
- **Cast**: silhouettes must read in solid black. One absurd costume idea each (goggles pushed up on a bald head; a bright helmet on a small kid with a big head). Non-verbal creatures and machines get one big eye each.
- **The portal** (any device between worlds) is the only thing that glows: a lumpy rim with a thick outline, rotating spiral arms, a pale core, orbiting sparks, a faint flat wash while it is open. It opens with a gentle overshoot (~10%, back-ease 0.3 s).
- **Screen lettering**: a retro terminal face (VT323) for boards and scoreboards.

## 3. Colour logic

- **One palette per world**, three to five colours, different from the previous world in hue and value so the jump reads from colour alone: `--latar` (the home room), `--aksen` (the strange world's ground), `--latar-2` (the suspiciously normal world).
- `--utama` is the portal's glow and nothing else may glow in it; it also fills the speaker pill and the sign-up button. `--aksen` fills a lead's jacket and the other speaker pill.
- Line colour follows `--teks`; eye white, pupils, skin, helmet red, cardboard and sweat blue stay fixed in every brand. Words on the wall use `--teks` or `--teks-redup`; the pill text uses `--teks-di-utama` / `--teks-di-aksen`. Subtitles are always white with a dark outline, whatever the world.
- A deliberately bland palette (beige) is itself a joke: use it for the calm world.

## 4. Type

- `--font-judul`: Fredoka 700, rounded and heavy, like the cartoon's own captions. Subtitles ~54 px at 1920 wide, white with a ~12 px dark outline and a small speaker pill (26 px) in the speaker's colour. Title cards 80–90 px, two lines at most.
- `--font-isi`: Fredoka 500 for small lines on the board (32–36 px).
- Terminal tags and scoreboard digits: VT323 at 100–130 px.
- Keep faces out of the subtitle band (bottom ~170 px). Wrap lines over ~1300 px.
- Timing: a subtitle holds `max(1.4 s, speech + 0.4 s)`; clear it **before a silent beat** so the silence plays on a clean screen.

## 5. Motion quality

- **Characters on twos (12 fps)**: poses, mouths, blinks, jitter and boil step at 12 fps. **Camera moves, portal swirl, flying props and wipes on ones**.
- **Acting over moving**: held poses with small changes: a pupil sliding 14 px, a gulp, sweat running 46 px in 0.8 s, breathing. Mouth open/closed swaps every 1/12 s while a line plays, with the open mouth squashed to a random 0.55–1.35 height.
- **Nervous jitter**: a 12 fps random offset of 3–6 px on the head, growing with panic. A word shake: a 24 fps random offset of ±9 px on the whole shot for 0.35 s.
- **Squash and stretch**: landings squash to 1.18 × 0.82 for 0.1 s and back; flying out of the portal stretches 1.3 tall; "sucked in" shrinks toward the portal centre in 0.25 s.
- Slow camera: a push-in of 4–6% over the length of the shot; a rush zoom into the portal reaches ×3.4 in 0.7 s on `power2.in`.
- Cut rhythm: shots of 1.4–3.8 s; the cold pause (a still close-up, a flat face) is ~1.5 s with nothing moving but the boil.

## 6. Camera grammar

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Medium two-shot, scene scaled about 1.5× on the pair | the relationship; the leads fill 70–80% of frame height with the busy lab around them | the opening; dialogue; a standoff; a deal |
| Camera cut to a face (same world, scale ~2.4×) | the close-up of each lead as the line lands; the drawing is not redrawn, only the camera moves | a reply; a worry; a deadpan beat |
| Hard cut to a close-up | an interruption, a face breaking | the cut-off line; a realisation; a lie |
| Insert extreme close-up of an object | the absurd detail | a reveal; the problem itself; the wrong result |
| Reaction close-up | the laugh lives on the face | after every absurd image |
| Tight close-up + shake on one word | panic | the key word; an alarm; a scream |
| Rush zoom into the portal, swirl wipe | leaving a world | a jump between places, times or versions |
| Same framing across worlds | only the world changes | a montage; a comparison; a list |
| Very slow push-in on a still shot | a cold silence | the pause after a reversal; a confession |
| Wide with the device and both leads | the whole situation; used only for the portal moment and the closing card | a callback; a trap; the sign-up card |

Open and close on medium shots and cut to a close-up for each face; keep the wide shot for the portal and for the final card. Medium shots drift in 5% over their length (scale 1.5 to 1.58), close-ups 4%. Every absurd image is followed by a reaction close-up. Transitions go through the portal (swirl wipes) or hard cuts; no dissolves.

## 7. Native moves

- **Parallel worlds.** Each jump gets a new palette and a new creature. *Fits content like:* versions of a product; careers you could have had; a school club's first match; the same street in five eras.
- **Duo contrast.** Deadpan against panic, the joke is the difference. *Fits content like:* a coach and a nervous student; a veteran and a new hire; a parent and a teenager; an assistant and its user.
- **Medium, then a face.** Open on a medium two-shot with the lab behind, then cut to the close-up of whoever answers. *Fits content like:* a club coach and a nervous student; a shop owner and a new hire; a lecturer and a doubtful class.
- **Hardware as junk.** World-bending tech used for a petty chore. *Fits content like:* a gate between worlds to deliver a cardboard robot; a rocket for a sandwich; a time machine to fix a typo.
- **The suspiciously normal world.** The pattern breaks and the calm is the joke. *Fits content like:* the one boring answer that works; a quiet classroom after chaos; the sign-up desk.
- **Dead-air reversal.** A long silence after the twist, then one flat line. *Fits content like:* a price reveal; fine print; a result nobody expected.
- **Callback button.** The last line echoes the first so the story loops. *Fits content like:* a brand's catchphrase; a running complaint; a morning routine.

## 8. Pitfalls

- A springy overshoot swallows the actors: keep the portal's back-ease gentle.
- Close-ups scaled up make fat lines: keep stroke width fixed in screen space.
- A cold pause with a moving background is not cold: only the boil may move.
- Food and liquids need cues (drips, steam) or they read as other objects.
- Do not pair acid green, slime drips and wobbly bubble lettering, which reads as one specific show.
- Dark brands: lines follow `--teks`, so they turn light on a dark wall; check that skin and eyes still read.

# Sci-fi cartoon: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 1.4, medium 2.4, long 3.6.

## hook

- en: medium two-shot of a deadpan lead and a nervous one, outlines boiling; a mundane gag plays out in the middle while they talk
- id: dua tokoh berdampingan, satu datar satu gugup, garis bergetar; gurauan kecil berjalan di tengah saat mereka bicara

## problem

- en: hard cut to a reaction close-up: wide eyes, sweat, trembling pupils and a shake on the key word
- id: hard cut ke close-up reaksi: mata melebar, keringat, pupil gemetar, dan guncangan pada kata kuncinya

## fact

- en: insert extreme close-up of the absurd detail, then a reaction close-up held on a flat face
- id: close-up ekstrem pada detail yang absurd, lalu close-up reaksi yang ditahan pada wajah datar

## step

- en: the glowing portal pops open with a small overshoot, rush zoom into it, swirl wipe into a world with a new palette
- id: portal bercahaya terbuka dengan lompatan kecil, zoom masuk cepat, swirl wipe ke dunia berpalet baru

## compare

- en: the same framing repeated across two worlds, only the palette and the creature change; one rejection line each
- id: bingkai yang sama diulang di dua dunia, hanya palet dan makhluknya yang berganti; satu kalimat penolakan tiap dunia

## number

- en: the figure on a retro terminal or scoreboard that flips in on twos, with a dead-air beat before anyone reacts
- id: angka di papan skor ala terminal retro yang berganti per dua frame, lalu jeda sunyi sebelum ada yang bereaksi

## proof

- en: a slow push-in on a still two-shot: the result sits there while the leads react differently
- id: zoom masuk sangat pelan pada dua tokoh yang diam: hasilnya terpampang sementara reaksi mereka berbeda

## offer

- en: the suspiciously normal world: calm beige palette, a small deadpan line, the offer lands without any gag
- id: dunia yang biasa saja: palet krem tenang, satu kalimat datar, tawaran jatuh tanpa gurauan

## cta

- en: calm room, title card popped in on twos on the board with the contact on a pill; still for 2 s, only the line boils
- id: ruang tenang, kartu judul muncul per dua frame di papan dengan kontak di pil; diam 2 detik, hanya garis yang bergetar

## payoff

- en: wide shot with both leads and the device in frame, the last line echoing the first; held 2 s
- id: bidikan lebar dua tokoh dan perangkatnya, kalimat terakhir menggema kalimat pertama; diam 2 detik

      const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
      const $ = (s) => document.querySelector(s), R = $("#root");

      const rect = (x, y, w, h) => [[x, y], [x + w, y], [x + w, y + h], [x, y + h]];

          shape(j, [[ex + s * 31, by + (o.bo ?? 0)], [ex - s * 25, by + (o.bi ?? 0)]], { closed: false, stroke: F, lw: 10, amp: 0.8 });
        });

        shape(H.mc, quad([-26, 58], [0, 58 + (o.sm ?? -8)], [26, 58], 10), { closed: false, stroke: F, lw: 7 });
